title: SOC2 prep scratchpad - control mapping drafts
content:
(personal scratchpad) SOC2 prep notes / quick brain-dump. 

Background/context:
- Working off the baseline from last year's readiness check (limited scope: hosted API + console). Now expanding to include Dedicated + Private (customer-managed).
- Main ask: map existing policies/processes to common SOC2 CC categories (CC1-CC7) and identify evidence buckets.
- Timeline: initial control inventory by end of Q4 2025, gap remediation backlog for Q1 2026, auditor kickoff targeted Feb 2026 (soft).

Open questions / items to clarify:
- Scope: do we include on-prem private customers who run our package? (likely only control ownership for our control plane; need legal to confirm) --> ACTION: ask legal (Noah).
- Third-party vendors: which suppliers require vendor risk assessment evidence (e.g., cloud infra, KMS provider)? Need list from infra.
- Encryption at-rest evidence: where are key rotation logs kept for Redwood-managed KMS? Does Dedicated use customer KMS?

High-level control mapping (draft):
- CC2: Communication and information
  - Policy: Security policy handbook (security-and-compliance/handbook) - evidence: current PDF + approval email
  - Control: Executive sponsor + quarterly review - owner: Ava / Noah - evidence: meeting notes, doc with version history

- CC6: Change management / logical access controls
  - Policy: Code deployment & CI/CD process (release-engineering) - evidence: CI run logs, PR approvals, deploy tags
  - Control: Access provisioning for PROD - owner: SRE / platform-eng - evidence: access request tickets (Okta/Jira), recertification logs
  - TODO: capture screenshots of Okta group membership page or export CSV (SRE to assist)

- CC7: System operations / availability
  - Policy: Incident response runbook + NOC rotation - evidence: incident postmortems, pagerduty rotation config
  - Control: SLA monitoring and alerting - evidence: Prometheus alert history, runbook links

Evidence buckets (where to collect):
- Policies & signed docs: confluence PDFs, Google Drive final copies (we should centralize copies in security repo)
- Access logs: Okta, GCP/AWS IAM logs, audit exports (rotate retention?)
- Deployment & change: GitHub PR history, CI artifacts, deploy tags
- Incidents: Postmortems in Drive + JIRA incidents, severity classification table
- Training: LMS completion CSV (security training), acknowledgement receipts (HR)

Immediate gaps I can see (quick):
- No centralized snapshot of user access recertifications in last 12 months. Okta has logs but no exported evidence package.
- KMS key rotation evidence: infra team uses cloud KMS; need rotation schedule & single-line export.
- Vendor inventory out-of-date: several small tools (Sentry, Logflare?) unclear whether vendor risk assessment exists.
- Dedicated/private scope clarity: control boundaries unclear between customer-managed and Redwood-managed pieces.

Action items / owners (very rough):
- Export Okta user group CSV + last auth time (owner: Liam) - due 2025-11-15
- Pull list of production service accounts + last used (owner: SRE team / Noah) - due 2025-11-20
- Compile vendor inventory + VRAs (owner: procurement/security) - due 2025-11-30
- Draft control narratives for CC6/CC7 (owner: Ava) - initial draft 2025-11-10
- Identify evidence locations & create evidence map doc (owner: Ava + Sofia) - start now, iterative

Notes on control narratives (brainstorm):
- Keep narratives short: what the control is, who performs it, frequency, where evidence lives, expected artifact name (standardize filenames).
- Example: "User access provisioning: Users onboarded via Okta SSO, requests via Jira onboarding template. Access granted by SRE team lead. Evidence: onboarding Jira ticket ID, Okta group change event, last recert export CSV."

Possible risks to call out to auditor early:
- Multi-tenant hosted API: rely on tenant isolation via namespaces + model routing; need to show logical separation and monitoring.
- Private deployments: data residency and control split — must define which controls Redwood retains vs customer for SOC scope.

Quick checklist for evidence collection (working):
- [ ] Centralized policy folder with approvals (security team)
- [ ] Access recertification export (Okta) - last 12 months
- [ ] List of service accounts & secrets owners
- [ ] CI/CD deployment approvals + signed release notes
- [ ] PM/Eng sign-off on on-call rota and incident postmortems (last 6 incidents)
- [ ] Encryption & KMS rotation schedule + logs
- [ ] Vendor inventory + evidence of vendor assessment for critical vendors
- [ ] Training completion reports (security hygiene)

Random notes / brainstorming snippets:
- Could we automate evidence exports monthly and store in a read-only bucket for auditors? (SRE/infra)
- For Dedicated: produce a standard "control boundary" doc customers get during onboarding. That helps show where Redwood controls end.
- Consider a lightweight evidence naming convention: SOC2-<control>-<artifact>-YYYYMMDD.pdf (makes auditor life easier)

Marked TODOs for next sync w/ security team (weekly):
- Walk through control mapping draft, assign final owners (Ava to run)
- Get legal confirmation on private-deployments scope
- Confirm auditor onboarding timeline & required formats (pdf vs raw exports)

References / links to seed docs (where I pulled initial assumptions):
- confluence://security/soc2-readiness-2024 (baseline)
- JIRA-SOC2-12 (task board)
- github.com/redwood-inference/security/docs/control-narratives (starter templates)

End of scratchpad. Will iterate; move to formal doc once owners assigned and evidence collected.
